clarifyingQuestions: Does lower or higher priority run first?
Should fairness override priority or only break monopoly?
Should cancellation remove immediately or mark stale?
How should canceled jobs interact with the fairness streak?
followUps: Add weighted fair queuing or priority aging so two busy tenants cannot starve a third lower-priority tenant.
Add worker pools and job resource classes.
Persist job state and cancellation events.
followUpGuide: For bounded-wait guarantees, combine the streak cap with priority aging (subtracting wait-time credit from effective priority) or maintain per-tenant virtual finish times under weighted fair queuing so two alternating high-priority tenants cannot starve a third tenant indefinitely.
For worker pools, split per-tenant and top-level heaps by capability class and enforce fairness inside each pool.
For durability, make `enqueue`, `cancel`, and `claim` state transitions transactional.
complexityAnalysis: - `enqueue` inserts into the tenant min-heap in O(log n_org) and updates the top-level tenant-head min-heap in O(log t) when the tenant's live head changes, where t is the number of active tenants and n is total queued entries.
- `cancel` records soft cancellation in expected O(1) hash-set time while keeping the job ID reserved until a positive-count `dispatch` reaps pending cancellations.

- Positive-count `dispatch(m)` reaps newly canceled IDs in O(c) expected time, lazily discards dead heap entries in O(log n) amortized per canceled entry, and selects each of the m dispatched jobs in O(log t + log n) amortized time using the top-level tenant-head heap and per-tenant heaps. Total work across n enqueues, c cancellations, and m dispatches is O((n + m) log n) worst-case (and O(n + m log t) when per-tenant arrivals already follow priority order), with O(n) space.
solutionGuide: Maintain one min-heap `(priority, sequence, job_id)` per tenant and a top-level min-heap `(head_priority, head_sequence, org)` of each active tenant's live head, tracking which sequence numbers are currently present in the top-level heap. Soft cancellations stay in `active_seq_by_id` until the start of a positive-count `dispatch`, which reaps canceled IDs into `dead_seqs` so their identifiers can be reused while stale heap entries are discarded lazily when popped. When `last_org` hits `max_consecutive`, set its popped head aside, query the best live head from any other tenant, and re-insert `last_org` if an alternate exists.
